en: Melting uses heat to change a solid to a liquid, whereas dissolving mixes solid particles evenly throughout a liquid solvent like water.
The air inside a balloon has mass, making a fully inflated balloon slightly heavier than a completely deflated one.
Liquid water evaporates into a gas at any temperature, not just when it reaches its boiling point of 100 degrees Celsius.
Rusting is a chemical change where iron reacts with oxygen and water to form a completely new substance called iron oxide.
Mercury is a liquid metal at room temperature, proving that not all liquid matter is water or a water-based solution.
When solid ice melts into liquid water, its total mass remains exactly the same because no matter is created or destroyed.
The bubbles forming in boiling water contain water vapor, not trapped air, because the liquid water is actively changing into a gas.
You can separate a solid mixture of iron filings and sand using a magnet without causing any chemical changes to the materials.
Sponge and rubber are solid materials that can be easily compressed, proving that not all solid matter is hard or completely rigid.
Water droplets on a cold glass exterior come from water vapor in the surrounding air condensing, not from liquid leaking through the glass.
Dissolved sugar does not vanish; it breaks into invisible particles that remain in the water and can be recovered by evaporation.
Burning wood is a chemical change that produces entirely new substances like ash and smoke, rather than just physically changing its shape.
